title: Multi-factor authentication coverage for workforce and administrators
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-003 requires AAL3-grade authenticators (hardware keys or device-bound non-exportable keys, no synced passkeys, two keys per user) for platform and sponsor privileged roles and AAL2 phishing-resistant authenticators for other workforce. SOC2-010 requires MFA. No workforce identity provider exists, so nothing is enforced.
target_answer: MFA is enforced at the workforce identity provider for every workforce and contractor account and every system federated to it, including email, source control, package registries, cloud consoles, CI/CD and support tools; systems that cannot federate are listed with their own MFA configuration evidence. All workforce authenticators are phishing-resistant (AAL2 minimum); platform privileged roles use AAL3-grade hardware or device-bound keys with two registered keys per person. There are no standing MFA exceptions; any temporary exception requires CISO approval, an expiry and a compensating control.
current_practice: Unknown for Echelon workforce systems; no evidence located. Target requirements exist in Unbound.
intended_practice: Select a workforce IdP that enforces phishing-resistant MFA by policy and enroll all personnel before production.
customer_statement: Echelon's design requires phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for all workforce access and hardware-backed keys for privileged roles. Enforcement through a workforce identity provider is planned; Echelon cannot yet evidence workforce MFA coverage.
residual_risks: Systems outside federation may retain weaker authentication.
open_questions: Do Echelon's current source control and package publishing accounts enforce MFA today? Not verified in this review.

title: Phishing-resistant authenticators and resistance to MFA bypass
status_rationale: CNV-PLT-003 prohibits synced passkeys for privileged roles and requires phishing-resistant authenticators for workforce; TVR-SEC-010 treats a synced passkey alone as insufficient for new recipients; CNV-PLT-011 requires accessible alternatives. Not implemented.
target_answer: Workforce users authenticate only with phishing-resistant authenticators (FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys or device-bound platform authenticators). Customer users are offered passkeys as the default and phishing-resistant options at no extra cost; SMS and voice codes are not offered for workforce and, for customers, are only a restricted fallback with compensating controls (cooling-off and sponsor-direct confirmation for high-risk actions). Synced passkeys are accepted for sign-in at AAL2 but are not sufficient alone for high-risk actions such as adding a new grant recipient. Push-based approval, if used, requires number matching. Session tokens are bound to the authenticated client where the platform supports it to reduce adversary-in-the-middle token theft. Accessible alternatives exist for users who cannot use device-bound authenticators.
intended_practice: Implement WebAuthn for all populations from the first release and treat other factors as restricted.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design makes phishing-resistant authentication (security keys and passkeys) the default, restricts SMS and voice codes, and requires stronger confirmation than a synced passkey alone for high-risk actions. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Session token theft by malware on the endpoint is not prevented by phishing-resistant authentication.
Account recovery may reintroduce phishable factors.

challenge.customer_intent: Stop account takeover of donors, advisors and staff.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Phished credentials and codes are used to redirect grants or steal personal data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional MFA (SMS, voice, TOTP, push) is widely bypassed by real-time phishing proxies, SIM swaps and push fatigue; it is far better than passwords alone but not phishing-resistant.
challenge.legally_required: FTC Safeguards Rule 16 CFR 314.4(c)(5) and NYDFS 500.12 require MFA for covered entities but do not mandate phishing-resistant factors; FFIEC 2021 guidance is supervisory and risk-based.
challenge.historical_convention: SMS and TOTP for customers; push for workforce.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Credential phishing and relay are eliminated in scope by origin-bound WebAuthn authenticators for any population that uses them exclusively.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: IdP policy and application configuration refuse weaker factors for workforce and for high-risk customer actions.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Authenticator type per authentication event is recorded and reportable.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Phishing-resistant by default for all populations, with restricted fallbacks guarded by cooling-off and sponsor-direct confirmation.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes; authenticator registrations and policy can be shown and tested.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely for workforce; uncertain for donor populations, where sponsors may resist anything that adds friction or excludes older donors.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If SMS or email recovery can reset a phishing-resistant authenticator without step-up and cooling-off.
challenge.alternative_cost: Hardware keys for privileged staff; support cost for donor enrollment.
challenge.alternative_risks: Accessibility exclusion; lockout when devices are lost; pressure to weaken recovery.
supporting_arguments: Origin binding defeats real-time phishing proxies.
Aligns with NIST SP 800-63-4 and CISA guidance on phishing-resistant MFA.
opposing_arguments: Customer populations include people without compatible devices.
Recovery paths are the residual weak point.

title: Customer federation: SSO via SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-IAM-001 provides for federated SponsorWorkforce and PartnerWorkforce realms; AUTH-I8 requires mapping by issuer plus subject or SCIM external ID, never email, with dual control on mapping changes; UNB-XIN-IAM-003 keeps step-up with a sponsor-controlled verifier. No implementation or protocol library selection exists.
target_answer: Unbound supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect federation for sponsor and partner workforce on all plans without a surcharge. Customers can require SSO-only sign-in and disable local credentials for their realm. Assertions are validated for signature, issuer, audience, recipient, time window and replay using a maintained library, with negative tests for known assertion attacks (signature wrapping, unsigned assertions, algorithm confusion). Identities are mapped by issuer plus subject, never by email; mapping changes need dual control and notice to the affected person. A compromised partner IdP can at most sign users into that partner's realm, and cannot satisfy step-up for high-risk actions, which uses a sponsor-controlled verifier.
intended_practice: Select a maintained federation library; implement validation negative tests; implement realm-scoped trust per IdP.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design supports SAML and OpenID Connect single sign-on, maps identities by immutable identifiers rather than email, and limits what a compromised partner identity provider can do. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Customer IdP misconfiguration (weak MFA at the IdP) is outside Echelon's control; this is a complementary user entity control.

title: Automated user lifecycle via SCIM and federated deprovisioning latency
status_rationale: AUTH-I8 references the SCIM external ID; TVR-WID-006 calls for a contractual maximum deprovisioning latency per partner tier; AUTH-I1 requires sessions and derived tokens to be invalidated or rechecked on authority change. Not implemented.
target_answer: Unbound exposes a SCIM 2.0 endpoint per customer realm, authenticated with a dedicated, scoped, rotatable credential and rate-limited, that can create, update and deactivate users and group-based role assignments but cannot create platform or sponsor-reserved privileged roles. Deactivation through SCIM revokes sessions, refresh tokens, API tokens and delegated agent grants for that principal on the next request, within a stated maximum latency that is a contractual term. Open items owned by a deactivated user (pending recommendations, approval tasks) are reassigned or held by sponsor policy, never silently executed.
intended_practice: Implement SCIM with scoped credentials; define and measure deprovisioning latency.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design supports SCIM provisioning and promises a defined maximum time from deprovisioning in the customer's identity system to loss of all platform access. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Customers that do not deploy SCIM rely on manual deprovisioning.
open_questions: What deprovisioning latency will be offered contractually per partner tier (TVR-WID-006 value is open)?

title: Password policy aligned to NIST SP 800-63-4 and credential storage
status_rationale: No password policy exists. CNV-PLT-003 directs authenticator strength but does not set a password policy. SEC-CRYPTO-001 requires approved cryptographic libraries.
target_answer: Passwords are optional for customers (passkeys are the default) and not used alone for workforce. Where passwords are used, the policy follows NIST SP 800-63B-4: length-based minimums with no composition rules, a generous maximum length, screening against breached and commonly used passwords, paste and password managers allowed, no security questions, no periodic forced rotation, and forced change on evidence of compromise. Passwords are stored with a memory-hard or iterated, salted password hashing function from an approved library. Online guessing is throttled per account and per source with bot detection, designed so that throttling cannot be used to lock legitimate users out at will. Where a customer contract or PCI-scoped context requires periodic rotation, the conflict is documented and resolved by MFA rather than rotation.
intended_practice: Implement 800-63B-4 password handling if passwords are supported at all.
customer_statement: Echelon plans to make passkeys the default and to follow NIST SP 800-63B-4 for any passwords: length-based rules, breached-password screening, no forced periodic rotation and strong salted hashing. Nothing is implemented yet.
residual_risks: Users reuse passwords across sites; breached-password screening only catches known breaches.
open_questions: Confirm exact numeric thresholds (minimum lengths for single-factor and multi-factor use) against the final published SP 800-63B-4 text before using them in customer materials.

challenge.customer_intent: Prevent password guessing and reuse attacks.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Account takeover through credential stuffing or cracked hashes.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Composition rules and forced 60 to 90 day rotation produce predictable passwords and user workarounds; NIST withdrew support for both.
challenge.legally_required: No US statute mandates composition or rotation for this context. PCI DSS 4.0.1 requires rotation or dynamic analysis only where passwords are the sole factor for in-scope systems, which Unbound is not expected to have.
challenge.contractually_required: Many bank questionnaires still ask for rotation intervals and complexity.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Password attacks are eliminated in scope for users who use passkeys only.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Policy is enforced in code; breached-password screening at set time.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Configuration and test results show policy; share of passwordless users is measurable.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Passwordless by default; 800-63B-4 rules where passwords remain; MFA everywhere.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by configuration review and tests.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely when the answer cites NIST SP 800-63B-4 explicitly; some assessors with legacy checklists will record an exception.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If passwords are the only factor for any population.
challenge.alternative_risks: Customer auditors with outdated checklists may record findings.
supporting_arguments: Current NIST guidance explicitly rejects forced periodic rotation and composition rules.
opposing_arguments: Legacy questionnaires and some internal bank standards still require rotation.

title: Session management, token handling and revocation
status_rationale: AUTH-I1 requires sessions, widget instances, partner tokens and agent privileges derived from changed authority to be invalidated or rechecked with a stated maximum staleness; UNB-RCN-ENT-004 suspends sessions on death or incapacity. Limen keeps browser storage and HTTP in its kernel; whether Unbound session tokens would be stored in browser-accessible storage is not decided. No session implementation exists.
target_answer: Browser sessions use opaque, server-side session identifiers in cookies marked Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite, never placed in browser-readable storage; new identifiers are issued at login and at any privilege change. Idle and absolute timeouts are risk-tiered (shorter for staff and privileged roles) and configurable by the sponsor within platform limits. Users and administrators can list and terminate sessions. Password, authenticator or contact changes, deactivation and authority changes revoke or recheck all sessions and refresh tokens within a stated maximum staleness. API refresh tokens rotate on use with reuse detection, and long-lived API tokens are scoped, expiring and revocable.
current_practice: Not implemented. Requirements exist for invalidation; token storage design is not decided.
intended_practice: Decide session architecture compatible with the Limen kernel boundary; implement revocation and timeouts.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design uses server-side sessions in protected cookies, risk-tiered timeouts, user-visible session management, and revocation of sessions when credentials or authority change. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Malware on the user's endpoint can use a live session regardless of cookie flags.
open_questions: Does the Limen kernel's storage capability need a rule forbidding session or bearer tokens in localStorage for Unbound?

title: Account recovery, authenticator changes and help-desk resets
status_rationale: AUTH-I7 requires step-up, a cooling-off period and notice to the prior channel for authority-relevant credential changes; CNV-PLT-011 requires prior-channel notification with a revert link, a default 72-hour hold on high-risk actions and an AccessibleAssurancePath; UNB-XIN-SVC-004 prohibits knowledge-based answers above the lowest assurance level and staff override of the contact assurance matrix; CNV-PLT-003 prohibits KBA for proofing and requires identity-proofed recovery for privileged roles. Not implemented.
target_answer: Recovery after loss of all authenticators requires re-proofing at the original assurance level (or a pre-registered second authenticator), never knowledge-based questions or email alone. Enrolling an authenticator, changing email, phone or recovery factors notifies the previous channel with a revert link and starts a cooling-off period (default 72 hours, sponsor-configurable) during which authority changes, successor changes and new-recipient grants above a threshold are held for confirmation. Support staff cannot reset authenticators or change contact details beyond the contact assurance matrix and cannot override it. Accessible recovery paths (mailed code, outbound call to a verified number, captioned assisted video, in-person or notarized verification, relay calls) each reach a defined assurance level.
intended_practice: Implement recovery, cooling-off and contact assurance matrix as part of the identity core.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design never uses security questions, notifies the previous channel on any credential or contact change, holds high-risk actions during a cooling-off period, and prevents support staff from overriding verification rules. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Cooling-off periods delay legitimate urgent grants; sponsors may press to shorten them.
Deepfake voice or video may defeat assisted verification.

challenge.customer_intent: Make sure attackers cannot take over accounts by convincing support or abusing recovery.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Help-desk social engineering resets MFA and the attacker redirects grants.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional recovery by security questions or email link is weak; agent verification scripts are routinely socially engineered.
challenge.legally_required: SEC Regulation S-ID requires covered firms to have identity theft red flags programs that address account changes; it binds covered broker-dealers and advisers, not Echelon, and only flows contractually.
challenge.historical_convention: Security questions, email reset, agent judgment.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Staff override is eliminated by enforcing the contact assurance matrix in the support tool; immediate post-change exploitation is eliminated by holds during cooling-off.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Holds and notifications are automatic and not discretionary.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Every change, notice, hold and release is an event.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Cooling-off with prior-channel revert plus sponsor-direct confirmation for new recipients.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through tests and event history.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely for banks and wealth managers familiar with holds after contact changes; donors may object to delays.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If any support or sponsor-staff path can waive the hold without independent approval.
challenge.alternative_risks: Attackers may change contacts and wait out the period; TVR-SEC-010 addresses this by measuring recipient novelty from the last pre-existing-channel confirmation.
supporting_arguments: The approach does not depend on staff detecting deception.
opposing_arguments: Accessibility and urgency exceptions create pressure to weaken holds.

title: Step-up authentication and transaction binding for high-risk and financial actions
status_rationale: UNB-XIN-IAM-003 defines a StepUpPolicy matrix (AAL2 phishing-resistant or AAL3 for privileged workforce, maximum authentication age default five minutes, step-up event bound to the command, verifier controlled by the sponsor not the partner IdP). TVR-SEC-004 bounds auto-approval by session assurance and requires step-up for new recipients from phishable or agent sessions. Not implemented.
target_answer: Each high-risk action class (authenticator or recovery change, authority or delegation change, payee or destination change, data export, grant recommendation above a sponsor threshold, API credential creation, sponsor policy publication) has a required assurance level and maximum authentication age in one StepUpPolicy matrix. The step-up event identifier is bound to the specific command and its parameters; a command without a fresh, matching step-up is rejected, and a step-up cannot be reused for another action. The step-up prompt shows the action's key details so the user confirms what will happen. Step-up is performed by a sponsor-controlled verifier, not delegated to a partner IdP. Auto-approval ceilings depend on session assurance, so a phishable or agent-initiated session cannot obtain an auto-approved grant to a new recipient. This implements the layered, risk-based approach of the FFIEC 2021 authentication guidance for the sponsor's and partner bank's customers.
intended_practice: Implement the StepUpPolicy matrix in the authorization core with command binding.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design requires fresh, phishing-resistant step-up authentication bound to each specific high-risk action, such as payee changes, large grant recommendations and data exports. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Man-in-the-browser malware may alter what is displayed; transaction detail display mitigates only if the authenticator or a separate channel displays the details.

title: Authentication of APIs, widgets, webhooks and AI agents
status_rationale: UNB-API-STD-005 requires each integration to document authentication method, credential rotation, least privilege, webhook signature verification, replay defense and partner context binding; AIN-029 requires embeds to independently authorize, expire safely and not impersonate the sponsor; TVR-WID-001 requires widget data cleared after authority revision change; TVR-SEC-004 treats agent sessions as needing step-up for new recipients. Not implemented.
target_answer: Partner and integration APIs use OAuth 2.0 client credentials or mutual TLS with per-client, scoped, expiring credentials; shared static API keys are not issued for new integrations. User-delegated API access uses OAuth authorization code with PKCE and scoped, short-lived access tokens. Embedded widgets run in an isolated origin and receive narrowly scoped, short-lived tokens never exposed to host-page scripts; they expire and clear data when authority changes. Inbound webhooks are signed, timestamped and replay-protected; outbound webhooks are signed. AI agents authenticate as their own Workload principals with delegated grants derived from a user, and an agent session is treated as lower assurance than a fresh human step-up for high-risk actions.
intended_practice: Define API authentication standards per UNB-API-STD-005 before the first integration.
customer_statement: Echelon's Unbound design uses scoped, expiring OAuth or mutual-TLS credentials for integrations, signed and replay-protected webhooks, isolated widget tokens, and separate lower-assurance identities for AI agents. This is planned, not operating.
residual_risks: Custodian and bank counterparties may support only legacy authentication.
